items.basis: Fortune Business Insights, Ice Cream Market Report: North America accounted for ~34% of global ice cream consumption/revenue share. Third-party market-research sizing (not a government or audited-company disclosure), hence grounded_estimate rather than real.

Fortune Business Insights, Ice Cream Market Report: Europe ~27% global share. Cross-checked against IMARC Group's independent estimate of ~35.1% for Europe for the same year — market-research firms diverge meaningfully on regional splits since no single body centrally measures global ice cream sales; this row uses the Fortune Business Insights figure for internal consistency with the other regions in this set.
Fortune Business Insights, Ice Cream Market Report: Asia-Pacific ~25% global share, cited as the fastest-growing region on rising disposable incomes and urbanization in China and India.
Fortune Business Insights, Ice Cream Market Report: Latin America ~9% global share.

Residual share (100% - North America - Europe - Asia-Pacific - Latin America) implied by the same Fortune Business Insights breakdown; not independently published as its own line figure by that source.

flags.headline: Store Brand sentiment declining
flags.body: Store Brand is currently the weakest performer in this dataset's brand sentiment, averaging 3.15/5 across 20 reviews sampled. At an assumed unit price, that sample represents roughly £60 of reviewed-unit retail value - illustrative of price-tier exposure in this sample, not total market sales.

dollar_estimate.basis: 20 sampled reviews x £3.00 assumed mass market tub unit price - illustrates this dataset's reviewed sample only, not total market sales

recommendation.action: Pull Store Brand's lowest-scoring reviews and tag the top 2-3 recurring complaints (flavor, texture, price, availability).
Run a targeted fix on Store Brand's weakest SKU - reformulation, price adjustment, or a promotion tied to the specific complaint, not the whole line.
If sentiment hasn't recovered, consider consolidating Store Brand into a stronger sibling line rather than continuing to invest evenly.

flags.headline: Production index up 5.4% MoM
flags.body: The production index reading for 2026-06 is 131.9 (2017=100), up 5.4% versus the prior month, and up 8.0% year-over-year. This is an index-based signal - no revenue anchor has been supplied for this panel, so no dollar figure is attached.

recommendation.action: Confirm current supply chain capacity can sustain this pace without rush freight or overtime costs eating the gain.
Pre-book raw material volumes at current prices before sustained demand pulls input costs up.
Evaluate a capacity increase only if the uptrend holds for another cycle.

kpis.spoilage_exposure_logic: Sum of units_on_hand × unit_cost_gbp for every region with weeks_to_expiry < 2.5 ("Spoilage risk").
kpis.spoilage_exposure_contributors: Contributing regions this cycle: Northern Ireland, North West.
kpis.cash_tied_up_logic: Sum of units_on_hand × unit_cost_gbp across all regions, regardless of status.
kpis.cash_tied_up_contributors: All 6 regions: London, Scotland, Wales, South East, Northern Ireland, North West.
kpis.equipment_exposure_logic: Sum of units_at_risk × unit_cost_gbp for every asset with failure_risk_pct ≥ 50.0%.
kpis.equipment_exposure_contributors: Contributing equipment this cycle: COMP-LON-01, CASE-WAL-02, TRK-SCO-03.
kpis.autonomous_actions_logic: Count and £ impact of activity-log entries auto-executed under the policy: impact < £75,000 AND confidence is real or grounded-estimate AND action type is not maintenance dispatch (that always requires human approval, regardless of size).
kpis.source: Illustrative UK retail client scenario (equipment_health.csv / regional_inventory.csv / demand_vs_plan.csv) — no public dataset of a real company's cold-chain telemetry exists; this demonstrates what the system computes once connected to a real client's real systems.

items.basis: Unilever FY2021 Full Year Results described Ice Cream growth as "mid-single-digit, balanced across volume and price" (~4.5% total) — exact split not separately disclosed that year; volume/price shown here assume an even split of the stated total, since Ice Cream was not yet broken out as its own reported Business Group in the original FY2021 filing.

Unilever FY2022 Full Year Results, Business Group performance table (Ice Cream): underlying sales growth +9.0%, comprising volume -0.7% and price +9.7% — Unilever's disciplined pricing action against input-cost inflation, with in-home volumes weak in Q4.

Unilever FY2023 Full Year Results, Business Group performance table (Ice Cream): underlying sales growth +2.3%, comprising volume -6.0% and price +8.8% — consumers downtrading to value formats amid high price elasticity; the clearest instance of price fully absorbing a volume decline in this window.

Unilever FY2024 Full Year Results, Business Group performance table (Ice Cream): underlying sales growth +9.8%, comprising volume +6.7% and price +2.9% — volume-led recovery as pricing normalized and promotional activity was optimized.
The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC) 2025 Full Year Results — first standalone report after the 2025-12-06 demerger from Unilever: organic sales growth +4.2%, comprising volume +1.5% and price +2.6%.

ice_cream_consumption_by_age.basis: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), citing National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) years 5 & 6: mean ice cream consumption 14g/day (2.9g/day sugar from ice cream specifically), equivalent to ~69 ice creams/year; ice cream contributes 5.8% of total diet sugar and 11.3% of sugar from the snacks category for this age group.
